sentences.text: In Norse mythology , Loki -LRB- Anglicized -LRB- -LSB- ˈloʊki -RSB- -RRB- -RRB- , Loptr , or Hveðrungr is a god or jötunn -LRB- or both -RRB- .	Norse mythology	Norse mythology	god	Æsir	jötunn	jötunn
Loki is the son of Fárbauti and Laufey , and the brother of Helblindi and Býleistr .	Fárbauti	Fárbauti	Laufey	Laufey	Helblindi	Helblindi	Býleistr	Býleistr
By the jötunn Angrboða , Loki is the father of Hel , the wolf Fenrir , and the world serpent Jörmungandr .	jötunn	jötunn	Angrboða	Angrboða	Hel	Hel (being)	Fenrir	Fenrir	Jörmungandr	Jörmungandr
By his wife Sigyn , Loki is the father of Narfi and/or Nari .	Sigyn	Sigyn	Narfi and/or Nari	Narfi and Nari
By the stallion Svaðilfari , Loki is the mother -- giving birth in the form of a mare -- to the eight-legged horse Sleipnir .	Svaðilfari	Svaðilfari	mare	mare	Sleipnir	Sleipnir

In addition , Loki is referred to as the father of Váli in Prose Edda , though this source also refers to Odin as the father of Váli twice , and Váli is found mentioned as a Son of Loki only once .	Váli	Váli	Prose Edda	Prose Edda	Odin	Odin
Loki 's relation with the gods varies by source ; Loki sometimes assists the gods and sometimes behaves in a malicious manner towards them .

Loki is a shape shifter and in separate incidents he appears in the form of a salmon , a mare , a fly , and possibly an elderly woman named Þökk -LRB- Old Norse ` thanks ' -RRB- .	mare	mare	shape shifter	Shapeshifting	salmon	salmon	fly	Fly (animal)	Þökk	Þökk

Loki 's positive relations with the gods end with his role in engineering the death of the god Baldr and Loki is eventually bound by Váli with the entrails of one of his sons .	god	Æsir	Váli	Váli	Baldr	Baldr
In both the Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda , the goddess Skaði is responsible for placing a serpent above him while he is bound .	Prose Edda	Prose Edda	Poetic Edda	Poetic Edda	Skaði	Skaði

The serpent drips venom from above him that Sigyn collects into a bowl ; however , she must empty the bowl when it is full , and the venom that drips in the meantime causes Loki to writhe in pain , thereby causing earthquakes .	Sigyn	Sigyn

With the onset of Ragnarök , Loki is foretold to slip free from his bonds and to fight against the gods among the forces of the jötnar , at which time he will encounter the god Heimdallr and the two will slay each other .	god	Æsir	Ragnarök	Ragnarök	jötnar	Jötunn	Heimdallr	Heimdallr

Loki is referred to in the Poetic Edda , compiled in the 13th century from earlier traditional sources ; the Prose Edda and Heimskringla , written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson ; the Norwegian Rune Poems , in the poetry of skalds , and in Scandinavian folklore .	Prose Edda	Prose Edda	Poetic Edda	Poetic Edda	Heimskringla	Heimskringla	Snorri Sturluson	Snorri Sturluson	Norwegian Rune Poems	Rune Poems

Loki may be depicted on the Snaptun Stone , the Kirkby Stephen Stone , and the Gosforth Cross .	Snaptun Stone	Snaptun Stone	Kirkby Stephen Stone	Loki#Kirkby Stephen Stone and Gosforth Cross	Gosforth Cross	Gosforth Cross

Loki 's origins and role in Norse mythology , which some scholars have described as that of a trickster god , have been much debated by scholars .	Norse mythology	Norse mythology	god	Æsir	trickster god	trickster god
Loki has been depicted in or is referenced in a variety of media in modern popular culture .
